newsitem.title: EGYPT: SOCCER-FIGHTING PROMPTS SUDAN'S CHAMPIONSHIP EXIT. [CORRECTED 16:01 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIGHTING PROMPTS SUDAN'S CHAMPIONSHIP EXIT. [CORRECTED 16:01 GMT]

text.p: Sudan have pulled out of the
African championship because of the fighting in the east of the country, the African soccer federation (CAF) said on Thursday.
Khartoum's withdrawal from the championship was due to "aggression on its eastern frontier and the consequent general mobilisation," CAF quoted Sudan's Football Association as saying.
Sudan have called for mobilisation against what they say are Ethiopian and rebel assaults on eastern Sudan, and they also accused neighbouring Eritrea of taking part in the fighting.
CAF said the Group One qualifying competition for next year's finals now comprised Zimbabwe, Ghana and Angola.
Sudan's withdrawal will come as a big blow to Zimbabwe, who beat them 3-0 away in the opening group match in October.
That result will now be deleted from the records, leaving Ghana top of the group.
Sudan were due to travel to Angola next weekend in the second round of qualifying for the finals in Burkina Faso next year.
Their withdrawal is the second from the qualifying after Burundi were disqualified last August for failing to turn up for a preliminary round match.
